10: ## User outcome
11: 
12: Jetpack users can manage all of their domains from one in-app flow. They can distinguish loading, empty, error, complete, and filtered states; recover failed loads; search for a new paid domain; choose whether to purchase it alone or attach it to an existing site; recover a failed cart submission; finish or cancel checkout; and safely view supported domain details without allowing arbitrary pages to remain inside the authenticated details web view.

14: ## Functional requirements
15: 
16: 1. Opening All Domains loads the account's domains and renders a distinct loading state followed by a complete list, an empty state, or a recoverable error state. A loaded row retains its domain identity, site title, status, expiry information, and details destination.
17: 2. The empty-state action and the add-domain action open the new-domain search flow. A list-load error exposes retry; retry enters loading again and replaces the error with the newly fetched result.
18: 3. Filtering an already loaded list is case-insensitive and can match the domain, site slug, or site title. Clearing the filter restores the same complete source list without refetching it or changing domain identity.
19: 4. New-domain search ignores blank input, waits 250 ms before dispatching a nonblank query, and keeps only the latest query when another query arrives while earlier work is pending. Stale results must not replace the latest result.
20: 5. Search results exclude free suggestions, retain product identifier, domain, price, optional sale price, and privacy support, and are ordered by descending relevance. A remote mismatch or failed suggestions response becomes an explicit error that can be retried with the retained query.
21: 6. Selecting a proposed domain opens a purchase-mode screen with that domain's product identifier and privacy capability. The user can purchase the domain alone or choose an existing site; these modes remain distinct through cart submission.
22: 7. Cart submission visibly distinguishes domain-only and existing-site progress, disables duplicate submissions while active, and routes a successful cart to the matching checkout or eligible plan flow. A failed cart shows an error, does not navigate, and can be acknowledged and retried from the same domain selection.
23: 8. A successful checkout and a user-cancelled checkout both return to All Domains through the production result path. A missing or invalid checkout result remains an error rather than being treated as completion.
24: 9. The in-app domain-details web view may remain on the matching `wordpress.com/domains/manage/all/<domain>/edit/...` path. Another host or another path is rejected from the contained web view and handed to the external-navigation path.

26: ## Failure and recovery
27: 
28: List, search, cart, and checkout failures are explicit states. Retry repeats the relevant application-owned operation with the retained user input. Older search completions cannot overwrite a newer query. Cart failure never launches checkout, and an invalid checkout result never reports completion. URL rejection preserves the domain-management screen while routing the unsupported destination outside the contained details view.

30: ## Invariants
31: 
32: - Filtering and remote search never mutate the account's stored domain list.
33: - Search results correspond to the latest normalized nonblank query.
34: - Product identifier, domain name, and privacy support remain attached to the selected proposal throughout purchase routing.
35: - A cart request is made at most once per explicit purchase attempt.
36: - Domain-only and existing-site cart modes never silently change into one another.
37: - Cancellation is not reported as a successful registration, even though both outcomes return to All Domains.
38: - The details web view never retains an unsupported host, domain, or path.
